name: hmac
title: Compute a hash-based message authentication code

origin.description: HMAC of a message with a secret key, using one of the digest hash functions.
origin.usage: hmac(key, object, algo = c("md5", "sha1", "crc32", "sha256", "sha512"), serialize = FALSE, raw = FALSE, ...)

arguments.name: key
arguments.text: A character or numeric vector used as the secret.

arguments.name: object
arguments.text: The message. Serialized only when serialize is TRUE.

arguments.name: algo
arguments.text: md5, sha1, crc32, sha256, or sha512. The examples pass one of these.

arguments.name: raw
arguments.text: If TRUE, return raw bytes instead of hex.

origin.details: The key is padded to the block size, 64 bytes except 4 for crc32 and 128 for sha512. A longer key is hashed first. The inner pad is xor with 0x36 and the outer pad is xor with 0x5c. The one-byte pad is recycled across the key.
origin.value: A hex string, or raw bytes when raw is TRUE.
origin.example: hmac('Jefe', 'what do ya want for nothing?', 'md5')

translation.description: HMAC of a message with a secret key.

arguments.name: key
arguments.text: A string, bytes, or a list of integers. A list of integers is as.raw.

arguments.name: object
arguments.text: The message. A string is charToRaw when serialize is False.

arguments.name: algo
arguments.text: md5, sha1, crc32, sha256, or sha512. A unique prefix is resolved by digest after the block size is chosen, so sha5 is sha512 and still uses a 64-byte block.

arguments.name: raw
arguments.text: If True, return bytes instead of hex.

translation.details: Block size is 64, except 4 for crc32 and 128 for sha512. A key longer than that is hashed. For crc32 the raw digest is turned back into bytes from its hex pairs, and a key longer than 4 bytes keeps the first byte of that digest. The inner pad is 0x36 and the outer pad is 0x5c.
translation.value: A hex string, or bytes when raw is True.
translation.example:
from digest import hmac
print(hmac("Jefe", "what do ya want for nothing?", "md5"))
